ex.1: Buys Ballot: in the S hemisphere with your BACK to the wind, low is on your right. Facing the wind, it is on your left.
ex.3: Local winds (land/sea breeze, katabatic, gusts) are driven by local effects and do not follow Buys Ballot's law; the book's key gives (a) False.
ex.12: N hemisphere: flying from high to low, the low is on your left so the wind comes from your right → starboard drift.
ex.13: Port drift = wind from the starboard side = flying towards high pressure → altimeter under-reads.
ex.17: Close isobars mean a steep pressure gradient and strong wind; the book's key takes it as parallel to the isobars.
ex.29: At night the friction layer shrinks, upper strong wind is cut off: surface wind backs and weakens (NH).
ex.37: Near the centre of a TRS Coriolis is negligible compared with the pressure gradient and centripetal terms: cyclostrophic balance.
ex.40: Warm south, cold north: thermal wind blows with cold (low thickness) on the left → westerly, increasing with height.
ex.41: In an anticyclone P = C + f, so the gradient wind is super-geostrophic: it is greater than (an over-estimate of) the geostrophic value.
ex.42: Gale = persistent mean wind of 34 kt or more (Beaufort 8), associated with depressions and cyclonic storms.
ex.44: With no pressure gradient, the flow balances centrifugal and Coriolis forces only: anticyclonic in both hemispheres.
